title: How Graceland Works
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant discuss Graceland, Elvis Presley's Memphis home, based on Chuck's HowStuffWorks article. They cover Matt Hale's Elvis-impersonator tour and Australian Elvis fan festival, the house's purchase from the YMCA-era owners and its name, the blocked-off upstairs and the untouched bathroom, the jungle room and TV room, the Lisa Marie jet and the Fool's Gold sandwich order, Elvis's pill use and money pressures, his 1970 meeting with Richard Nixon, and his burial in the meditation garden. The episode closes with a plug for Chuck's article and a Frogs article aside.

segments.title: Opening banter and Elvis impersonators
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the show, joke about Chuck's Elvis impression, and discuss Matt Hale, a British radio producer who toured the world dressed as Elvis and placed last at an Australian Elvis impersonator contest.

segments.title: Purchase and name of Graceland
segments.summary: Chuck describes the house's modest exterior and its late-1950s classic revival style. Elvis bought it at age 22 for about $102,000, outbidding the YMCA. The house was already named Graceland, after the original owners' great aunt Grace, and it sits on fourteen acres just south of downtown Memphis.

segments.title: Interior, foyer and upstairs retreat
segments.summary: The hosts describe the 1970s-style decor and the foyer, which sits beneath the bathroom where Elvis died. The upstairs was closed to guests in his lifetime and remains closed, and his bathroom has been left untouched since his death.

segments.title: Jungle room and TV room
segments.summary: The jungle room, originally a screened-in porch converted after Elvis's divorce from Priscilla, has African-style decor and shag carpeting and was where he recorded music. The downstairs TV room has three TVs built into the wall, an idea Elvis reportedly took from President Lyndon Johnson.

segments.title: Lisa Marie jet and Fool's Gold sandwich
segments.summary: Elvis owned two jets, including a Boeing 707 called the Lisa Marie. In February 1976 he ordered about thirty Fool's Gold sandwiches from a Denver restaurant, and they flew out to get them. The late-night trip reportedly cost around sixteen thousand dollars.

segments.title: Elvis's spending, touring and pill use
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how Elvis felt obligated to his large staff, which drove a punishing touring schedule and reliance on pills. His album sales declined later, and touring, including Vegas shows, became his main income.

segments.title: Elvis and Nixon meeting
segments.summary: Elvis wrote to Richard Nixon offering to act as an undercover Federal Bureau of Narcotics agent to infiltrate hippie and radical groups. After persistent pressing, Nixon met him, and Elvis gave Nixon a commemorative pistol and received an honorary badge. The hosts note the irony given Elvis's own drug use and that he drew a line between illegal and prescription drugs.

segments.title: Elvis's burial place
segments.summary: Elvis is buried in the meditation garden on the Graceland grounds, along with his mother, father and grandmother. He and his mother were first buried elsewhere, and his father moved them due to security concerns.

segments.title: Sign-off and frog article aside
segments.summary: Chuck recommends his Graceland article and the hosts plug the Are There Really Hallucinogenic Frogs? article, with Chuck mentioning his college frog collection. The show closes with an ad for the Camry.
